planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with roots kept cool and shaded; this high-elevation Chinese species benefits from a position among rocks or at the edge of light woodland rather than full baking sun.

directions: Clematis gracilifolia is a modest-sized climber native to rocky slopes and forest margins from eastern Tibet through western Sichuan and Yunnan into central China at elevations above 2000 meters, where it scrambles to only 6-12 feet rather than engulfing a tree. In late spring it produces flat, slightly fragrant, pure white flowers typically with four tepals, borne singly or in small clusters of two to five among the leaves of the previous season's growth. Its naturally restrained size suits a small trellis, low fence, or large container better than the rampant montana-group species, and it tolerates acid, neutral, or alkaline soils in sun or light shade as long as the root zone stays cool.

planting.note: Plant in a sheltered, south- or west-facing spot against a wall or sturdy fence; this evergreen species is more cold-sensitive than C. armandii and benefits from winter protection outside its mild-climate comfort zone.

directions: Clematis fasciculiflora is a vigorous evergreen climber from southwest China with leathery, pinnate leaves that emerge grey-green with purplish margins and can flush bronze in cold weather, some forms showing attractive silver marbling along the veins. In late winter it bears clusters of fragrant, nodding, bell-shaped creamy-white flowers, giving an early-season display similar in spirit to C. armandii or C. cirrhosa but with more distinctly mottled foliage. Give it a sturdy support such as a wall, fence, or arbor to climb by twining leaf stalks, and keep the root zone shaded and cool while the top growth reaches into full sun.

planting.note: Plant in spring where it can climb into a tree, shrub, or sturdy fence by twining leaf stalks; some collected forms of this wide-ranging species have proven considerably more cold-hardy than its tropical and subtropical native range would suggest.

directions: Clematis gouriana is a vigorous deciduous climber native from the Indian subcontinent through south-central China to the Philippines and New Guinea, scrambling by twining leaf stalks up into tree canopies in the wild. From late summer into fall it produces much-branched panicles of small, fragrant, greenish-white flowers made up of four downy sepals rather than true petals, followed by feathery seed heads typical of the genus. Give it a substantial tree, arbor, or fence to climb, full sun, and average well-drained soil; its wide native range means some sourced forms tolerate considerably colder winters than its subtropical reputation implies.

common_name: Picton's Variety Clematis (Mid-Pink Scented Montana Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; like other montana selections it needs a large, sturdy support to climb.

directions: Raised by the English nurseryman Percy Picton, Picton's Variety bears small, scented, mid-pink to light purple-mauve flowers in a single heavy spring flush, true to the montana group's bloom habit on the previous year's growth. Prune only immediately after flowering, since winter or spring pruning would remove the coming display, and give it a large wall, pergola, or mature tree to scramble across, as it shares the considerable vigor typical of montana selections.

common_name: Jenny Keay Clematis (Semi-Double White-Green Montana Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; less rampant than typical montana forms, it still benefits from a sturdy fence or wall.

directions: A chance seedling named for Alister Keay's wife, Jenny Keay produces large double to semi-double flowers that open white to pale green in shade and take on a pink tinge in sun, with shorter internodes and noticeably less rampant growth than typical montana forms. Like other montana selections it flowers in a single spring flush on the previous year's growth, so prune only right after bloom, and give it a medium-sized fence or wall rather than the vast tree or pergola needed by more vigorous montana cultivars.

common_name: Peveril Clematis (White Montana Clematis with Yellow Anthers)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Peveril needs a large, sturdy support typical of montana-group vigor.

directions: Peveril bears white, four-sepaled flowers roughly three inches across, each centered on a prominent boss of creamy filaments and yellow anthers, in the single heavy spring flush typical of the montana group. It flowers on the previous year's growth, so prune only immediately after bloom to control size, and provide a large, sturdy wall, pergola, or mature tree, since it shares the considerable mature vigor of other montana selections.
